cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved and painted wooden speaker's staff with potlatch-ring hat figures, copper form, and crest imagery — a ceremonial regalia object consistent with Northwest Coast (Heiltsuk) traditional use, plausible for the claimed culture.

physical.title: staff
physical.summary: Painted and carved wood speaker's staff [?]. From top to bottom the figures and forms are: a wedge shaped painted finial, perhaps representing a spear point, decorated with simple geometric designs, followed by a cylindrical [spear shaft?] section; over a head, with a cylindrical section underneath, joined to the potlatch rings of a hat, sitting on the head of a complete figure; below is a short cylindrical section, and a three dimensional copper form, the upper section on one side carved with a human head in high relief; followed by a cylindrical section joining into the hat rings of a second figure, which follows onto the head of a hawk [?], followed by a final cylindrical section.
